# Desktop Monkey

> A free, open-source pixel-art desktop pet for Windows and macOS. He follows your
> mouse cursor around the screen, and when the mouse sits still he gets on with his
> own life — wandering, climbing the screen edge, napping, eating, and leaving poop
> on your wallpaper. One 6 MB file, no installer, no account, no dependencies.

## Facts

- **Platforms**: Windows 10/11 (single .exe, no installer) and macOS (Homebrew cask, signed and notarized by Apple)
- **Price**: free, and free forever. No account, no telemetry, no in-app purchase
- **License**: MIT for the code. Sprites belong to their authors (tiki-ted, Reactorcore) and are not covered by it
- **Written in**: Go — no game engine. Windows uses user32 syscalls without cgo; macOS uses Cocoa/CoreGraphics
- **Size on disk**: about 6 MB
- **Updates**: the app updates itself from GitHub releases
- **Languages**: English by default, French auto-detected from the system language, and forceable in settings
- **Made by**: My-Monkey (https://my-monkey.fr), a French non-profit collective based in Montpellier

## What he actually does

- Follows the mouse cursor everywhere, and hunts it down to whack it with a banana — a hit knocks the real cursor across the screen
- Takes clicks: three hearts, a damage flash, then he keels over onto the taskbar. Shake his body to revive him
- Climbs the screen edge, admires the view, then drops — the landing costs him a heart
- Eats, digests, then poops on the wallpaper. Click a poop to pop it. He also cleans up old ones, sometimes by throwing them at your cursor
- Naps for real, with floating Z's, and any mouse movement startles him awake
- Runs on four mood gauges — energy, boredom, happiness, fear — that drift with how you treat him and weight everything he does
- Can be tickled by shaking the mouse right next to him

## Common questions

- **He died. How do I revive him?** Grab the body and shake it. He comes back a bit jittery.
- **He's too big.** Tray menu → Open settings → Size, anywhere from 0.5× to 3×.
- **Does he speak French?** Yes. He follows the system language, and it can be forced in settings.
- **How do I uninstall him?** `brew uninstall --cask desktop-monkey` on macOS, or delete `monkey.exe` on Windows.

## Also from My-Monkey

Other things by the same collective:

- [OpenSuperWhisper](https://opensuperwhisper.com) — voice dictation for macOS. Hold a shortcut, speak, release, and the text lands in whatever app you are in. Four transcription engines, three of them fully on-device. MIT, source at https://github.com/my-monkeys/OpenSuperWhisper
- [Monkey Claude Usage](https://github.com/my-monkeys/monkey-claude-usage) — every Claude account you own, metered in the macOS menu bar: session, weekly and per-model limits, with a countdown once one is spent. BSD-2-Clause.
- [Monkey Battery](https://github.com/my-monkeys/monkey-battery) — how long a Mac really has left on battery, shown next to the battery icon below 10 %, with a red panel and an alarm two minutes before it sleeps. BSD-2-Clause.
- [GeoDaily](https://geodaily.eu) — a daily geography quiz in the browser, with practice modes for every continent and leaderboards.
- [Glance](https://glance-analytics.com) — a client for Umami and Plausible analytics: every site on one screen, live visitors, charts. iOS, Android, macOS and Windows. MIT.
